judged_text: Attendees are persisted (prisma.booking.update createMany) before the calendar update and email fan-out, and the dedupe filter treats already-stored emails as invalid input, so any failure after the write makes the exact same guest list permanently un-retryable. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)` (which is wrapped in a `try/catch` that swallows errors and still returns success). The dedupe logic for retries (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` and `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw BAD_REQUEST`) means that if anything fails after the DB write (notably `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is not caught, or emails, which are caught/ignored), the same email list will be filtered out on retry because they now already exist in `booking.attendees`, making the operation non-retryable through this flow and potentially leaving guests persisted without downstream side effects (calendar/email). This is directly supported by the ordering and conditions shown in the diff.
